_comment: Permission policy for edullm-reservoir-publish — the role that runs `publish()` for
pretrain/reservoir-dolma2 on AWS Batch, in-region.
WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS AT ALL, rather than reusing edullm-reservoir-ingest. That role's
`NeverWriteValidatorTriggeringOrTerminalNames` statement explicitly DENIES PutObject on
`*manifest.json` and `*dataset.json` anywhere in edullm-landing — which are exactly the two
objects publish() must write (publish.py:785 reserves the version with a create-only
dataset.json, publish.py:813 writes each group's manifest.json). Its Allow is also scoped to
`_ingest/reservoir-dolma2/*`, and publish() copies payload to `<dataset_id>/<version>/`, which
is outside that prefix. So the build role cannot publish, deliberately: a builder that could
write a manifest could fire the validator against a half-built prefix.
The reverse of the build role's Deny is the whole point here, so this role is the ONLY one in
the reservoir line permitted those two basenames, and only under the dataset's own prefix.
STILL NO WRITE TO edullm-data. That bucket is writable solely by the validator role, and that
is the airlock — an IAM Deny in 02-bucket-policy.json, not a convention. publish() only ever
stages into landing; promote() is the validator's job. Read access to edullm-data is needed
because publish() reads the published tokenizer (to bind tokenizer/dolma2-bpe) and the catalog
to pick the next version.
GetObject on the build prefix is required and is NOT redundant with the copy: publish()
stream-hashes every source object to compute the manifest sha256 (which is why it must run
in-region — it pulls every byte to wherever it runs; measured at 0.8 MiB/s off-region, ~9 days
for 587 GiB). The copies themselves are server-side and need read on the source plus write on
the destination, both of which are in landing here.
